details: CONFIRMED by running a copy of bin/check in a throwaway repo (evidence). Lines 24-37: any first argument other
than --tests is taken as the task form, and TEST_FILES then comes from the environment (normally empty), so pytest
gets no file and collects everything. Relay has no openspec/ folder, so the task form can never name a real task;
the only form relay can serve is --tests, and the others must refuse. Reachable: kit_packet_rules.md tells a worker
to "Loop on the quiet check (gate.check; when it takes a change and a task, run it for yours ...)", and the queue
item's own Why records a brief that named bin/check; a worker that now finds bin/check and calls it bare or with a
slug and a task waits 5 minutes for a HUNG and spends a round. The time for the whole suite under one pytest
process is not measured (only the gate's parallel 607 s), so HUNG is PLAUSIBLE; the wrong form handling is CONFIRMED.
Size: 15 agent minutes (an argument check before KEY, two tests in tests/test_own_gate_scripts.py).
evidence: $ cd <tmp repo with bin/check, test_x.py, test_y.py>; bin/check; echo rc=$?
$ ls <worktree>/openspec -> No such file or directory
failing_case: In a repo holding relay's bin/check, test_x.py (passes) and test_y.py (fails):
bin/check                -> runs both files, "FAILED at tests (round 1 of 3; log: .ci/check/task-tests.log)", exit 1
bin/check nochange 9.9   -> runs both files, "FAILED at tests (... task-9.9.log)", exit 1
bin/check --tests        -> pytest with no file: the whole suite
In relay itself each of these is `pytest -q -x` over all 154 test files in one process (the gate needs 607 s in
parallel), bounded by CHECK_TIMEOUT 300 s: a HUNG line after 5 minutes, counted as a failed round.
Should: exit 2 with a usage line and run nothing (README "The check-script contract", Behaviour 2: "2 for a usage
error, an unknown change or task, or a task with no Check: command; nothing was run").
fix_hint: Before KEY is set: if ARGS[:1] != ["--tests"] or not [a for a in ARGS[1:] if a != "--failed"]: print
"usage: bin/check --tests <file>... [--failed] (relay has no OpenSpec tasks)" to stderr and sys.exit(2).
Add the bare and no-file cases to tests/test_own_gate_scripts.py (exit 2, no .ci/check/*.log).
pass_cases: 1. bin/check (no arguments) -> exit 2, a usage line naming `bin/check --tests <file>... [--failed]`, no .ci/check/*.log written, no pytest run.
2. bin/check --tests (no file) -> exit 2, usage line, nothing run.
3. bin/check some-change 1.1 (relay has no openspec/changes) -> exit 2, a line saying relay's check takes --tests <file>... (or "no change 'some-change'"), nothing run.
5. bin/check --tests test_y.py (failing) -> exit 1, "FAILED at tests (round 1 of 3; ...)" (today's behaviour, keep).
reason: tests/test_own_gate_scripts.py:46 test_usage_errors_run_nothing passes, fails on base.
findings.summary: bin/check with no arguments or with <change> <task> runs every test instead of exiting 2 (contract: usage error), so in relay it runs the whole suite and ends HUNG after 300 s

details: PLAUSIBLE (not run: mypy is missing on this machine, doctor shows "FIX mypy 1.18.2", so bin/types-lint would fail
here today). Relay's gate runs bin/types-lint first (1 s). Adding it makes the quick check match the contract and
the gate's first step; the cost is that bin/check then needs mypy installed, which doctor already asks for. LOW:
the gate still catches the error, one round later. Size: 5 agent minutes.
evidence: .relay/checks/87f2434c...gate.log: "ci: types and lint ok (1s)" is the gate's first step.
bin/check:104 run_step("tests", ["pytest", "-q", "-x", *TEST_FILES]) is the only step.
failing_case: A fixer adds a function with an unused import (ruff F401) or a type error in a strict module, then runs
bin/check --tests tests/test_x.py -> "passed"; the gate's first step "ci: types and lint" then fails.
README contract: "--tests <file>...: review-fix mode: the quick steps, then these test files".
fix_hint: run_step("types and lint", [os.path.join(ROOT, "bin", "types-lint")]) before the tests step (or record in the comment
that relay's check is tests only, by choice).
pass_cases: 1. bin/check --tests <passing file> with an unused import added to lib/relay_x.py -> exit 1, "FAILED at types and lint".
2. bin/check --tests <passing file> on a clean tree -> exit 0, "passed".
3. bin/check --tests <failing file> on a clean tree -> exit 1, "FAILED at tests".
reason: tests/test_own_gate_scripts.py:54 and :59 pass; fail on base.
findings.summary: --tests runs only the test files, not the quick steps (types and lint) the contract names, so a fixer's green check can still fail the gate's types-and-lint step
